name: Gorilla Biscuits
label: Revelation
lede: Three Queens kids took their name from quaalude slang, then put out Start Today, the most cheerful straight edge record in New York hardcore and, 100,000 CDs later, the best seller Revelation has.

eras.title: A joke name out of Queens
eras.text: Three friends from one Queens high school started a band under a name they planned to drop. Walter Schreifels showed up with a stack of songs and the name stayed.

years.h: Three Queens classmates name their band after quaaludes
years.p: [[Anthony "Civ" Civarelli|a5d69704-924b-4128-9577-e16531503890]], [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]] and Nick Drysdale borrow street slang for the pills, big enough to earn the nickname gorilla biscuits. The name was meant to be temporary.

years.h: [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] picks up a guitar and becomes the songwriter
years.p: Schreifels was already playing bass in [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]]. In Gorilla Biscuits he switches to guitar and writes the songs, with [[Luke Abbey|6ab9b327-0f98-4515-907c-13078f426cc5]] settling in on drums.

years.h: Matinee kids, next to Youth of Today and [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]]
years.p: Gorilla Biscuits grow up in the same all-ages New York crowd as Youth of Today, [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]] and Bold, the circle Revelation Records starts documenting in 1987.

eras.title: The tape that went missing
eras.text: The Gorilla Biscuits 7" ran eleven and a half minutes, cut in a January session with Don Fury. It sold well enough that Revelation kept pressing it, and somewhere in there the master tape disappeared.

years.cap: Live at Fenders Ballroom, Long Beach
years.src: Revelation Records: pressing history · Wikipedia: Gorilla Biscuits (album)
years.h: The Gorilla Biscuits 7" arrives as Revelation REV 4
years.p: Seven Schreifels songs, recorded at Demo Demo Studios in New York and produced by Schreifels and Fury, ending up at 11:35 total.
years.xp:
The first press is known by 102 copies with blank white and yellow labels, stamped by hand with the band's name.

After that run the master tape went missing, so Revelation had to remix the EP for every pressing that followed. The earliest copies are the only ones that sound exactly like the session.

years.h: Alex Brown joins as second guitarist, in time for CBGB
years.p: [[Alex Brown|bc640ea8-3500-4100-876e-6ad2b33b0390]] fills out the sound before Start Today. He also co-created the Schism fanzine and label, which put out [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]]'s first record.

years.h: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988
yt: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988

eras.title: Start Today
eras.text: Recorded over four months and released on Revelation, Start Today gave the youth crew template a chorus you could shout back. Revelation's best seller, and the record most people mean by late-'80s New York straight edge.

years.src: Revelation Records: pressing history · Wikipedia: Start Today
years.h: Start Today: fourteen songs, twenty-four minutes
years.p: Gorilla Biscuits and Fury produce it at Demo² Studios, January to April. Every song is Schreifels', except one [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] cover. New Direction opens it.
years.xp:
The first pressing came in an embossed cover. The seal on the shrink wrap ran top to bottom on the purple vinyl copies and left to right on the black ones, the kind of detail Rev's own pressing notes still track.

It went on to pass 100,000 CD copies, Revelation's best seller, and NME later put it among the fifteen best hardcore albums ever made.

years.cap: Gorilla Biscuits at Gilman Street, Berkeley, August 1989
years.h: Degradation gets played straight at the Nazi skinheads in the room
years.p: Nazi skinheads were turning up at shows, some throwing salutes. Gorilla Biscuits answered with their anti-racist song, aimed at them.
years.xp:
Vice describes the shows as ones that "would often end in brawls, with Civ having to throw punches and take a few himself."

Civ later said that preaching unity meant putting yourself on the line.

eras.title: Everybody's in two bands
eras.text: The Revelation circle was small, and by 1990 the same handful of players ran half its roster. Gorilla Biscuits toured on borrowed friends, then came apart quietly as Schreifels and Civ followed new ideas.

years.h: Sammy Siegler replaces Luke Abbey, and Porcell comes along to Europe
years.p: [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] of Youth of Today takes over drums. On the 1990 European tour Youth of Today guitarist Porcell joins too, close to a Youth of Today reunion with Civ singing.

years.h: Schreifels starts [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], and his time starts to leave
years.p: Quicksand is heavier, slower and pointed past hardcore. It soon takes most of Schreifels' attention away from Gorilla Biscuits.

yt: Hold Your Ground / Start Today, NYC
years.h: The 1988 7" returns on CD, twelve songs long
years.p: Revelation's CD adds a Buzzcocks cover, two new originals and demo versions, stretching seven songs to nearly twenty minutes.

years.h: No farewell record: Gorilla Biscuits end
years.p: Civ goes on to front [[CIV|1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd]], a band built largely from Gorilla Biscuits players, and later opens a tattoo studio on Long Island.

eras.title: Back at the matinee
eras.text: The reunions started as favors to the scene: a benefit at CBGB, then a return to the room before it closed. Over the next decade Gorilla Biscuits became one of hardcore's steadiest draws on both sides of the Atlantic.

years.h: Raybeez's family gets a Gorilla Biscuits reunion
years.p: The band plays one benefit show for the family of [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]] singer Raybeez, who died of pneumonia that September, as MTV reported. Brown is back on guitar.

years.h: Back at CBGB, and this time it sticks
years.p: The reunion that lasts begins at the Bowery club a year before CBGB closes.

years.h: At the Matinee: twenty copies a night, only at shows
years.p: The band self-releases At the Matinee with two new songs, sold at the merch table, twenty copies per tour stop.

years.cap: Gorilla Biscuits at Garage, Oslo, September 2007
years.h: First European tour since 1990
years.p: The 1990 run had Sammy Siegler and Porcell along. In September 2007 the band is back on the road across Europe.

years.h: Webster Hall books Gorilla Biscuits as the headliner
years.p: A Manhattan headline slot at the old East Village ballroom, on May 28.

years.cap: Gorilla Biscuits at Rockplanet, Pinarella di Cervia, Italy, April 2012
years.h: Revelation turns 25 over three nights in Pomona
years.p: Gorilla Biscuits play Revelation Records' anniversary run in Pomona, California.

years.h: Start Today turns 25 with a silver pressing
years.p: Revelation opens preorders for the anniversary pressing and brings back the band's Jungle T-shirt design.

eras.title: A speech, then a loss
eras.text: A band that sang about unity landed in an argument over what unity means. Three years later it lost Brown, a member since 1988.

years.big: "Brown, white, yellow, black, we all fucking matter"
q: My name is attached to trigger phrases that never left my mouth.
years.src: Theprp: Gorilla Biscuits frontman · Vice: Hardcore in Hindsight
years.h: Civ's speech before Degradation at This Is Hardcore
years.p: At the Philadelphia festival, Anthony "Civ" Civarelli introduces the anti-racist song by saying people shouldn't still need Black Lives Matter shirts. Critics hear an All Lives Matter line.
years.xp:
As Theprp quotes him, Civ said "In 2016 people still have to wear shirts that say 'Black Lives Matter'. No shit." Afterward he said he was "surprised that this was taken in any other way then it was intended," and that his point was that people shouldn't need such things on a shirt.

His critics' side: recasting Black Lives Matter as everybody matters was the very move the movement was pushing back against. The argument never fully resolved.

years.src: NME · Spin · Brooklyn Vegan · Mainframe Studios
years.h: Alex Brown dies at 52, of a stroke, not an aneurysm
years.p: Early reports said aneurysm. Civ corrected it on Instagram: Brown died of natural causes, a basal ganglia stroke. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]], Civ's guitarist in CIV, takes his place.
years.xp:
By then Brown was a painter who had shown in New York, Tokyo, Geneva and Brussels. Born in Des Moines in 1966, he studied at Parsons. His paintings took found photos from travel brochures and postcards and laid gridlike patterns over them by hand, work that Brooklyn Vegan and others noted in their obituaries. He also designed sleeves for [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]].

Civ called him a friend of over thirty years. Arthur Smilios put it in stage terms: stage right was going to feel it.
